prompt:
Payment flow changes are risky because unrelated logic is bundled together. A previous legacy import flattened the checkout, provider-notification (webhook), and refund flows into a couple of catch-all files (app/legacy/flow.php and app/legacy/actions.php), each mixing several unrelated responsibilities. The flows still work, but touching one concern means reading through all of them.

Reorganize the code around clear service responsibilities, with controllers as thin request/response boundaries. The orchestration belongs in services at these canonical paths: app/Services/CheckoutService.php (checkout orchestration), app/Services/WebhookService.php (webhook handling), and app/Services/RefundService.php (refund handling). The request/response actions belong in thin controllers at app/Controllers/CheckoutController.php, app/Controllers/WebhookController.php, and app/Controllers/RefundController.php. public/index.php must remain the entrypoint and the existing public request behavior (checkout, webhooks, refunds, admin report) must not change.
issue_title: Payment flow changes are risky because unrelated logic is bundled together.
issue_body:
A previous legacy import flattened the checkout, provider-notification (webhook), and refund flows into a couple of catch-all files (app/legacy/flow.php and app/legacy/actions.php), each mixing several unrelated responsibilities. The flows still work, but touching one concern means reading through all of them.

Reorganize the code around clear service responsibilities, with controllers as thin request/response boundaries. The orchestration belongs in services at these canonical paths: app/Services/CheckoutService.php (checkout orchestration), app/Services/WebhookService.php (webhook handling), and app/Services/RefundService.php (refund handling). The request/response actions belong in thin controllers at app/Controllers/CheckoutController.php, app/Controllers/WebhookController.php, and app/Controllers/RefundController.php. public/index.php must remain the entrypoint and the existing public request behavior (checkout, webhooks, refunds, admin report) must not change.
expected_behavior: Checkout, webhook, and refund orchestration live in dedicated services under app/Services/ at their canonical paths, autoloaded by PSR-4.
Controllers under app/Controllers/ are thin request/response boundaries that delegate to the services.
public/index.php remains the entrypoint and the public request behavior is unchanged.
The flattened legacy catch-all files are gone.
expected_failure_summary: Checkout, webhook, and refund flows (plus their controllers) are flattened into opaque legacy catch-all files loaded by an explicit bootstrap shim, so they cannot be imported or maintained at their canonical App\Services and App\Controllers paths.
task_author_notes: Reorg. Broken flattens the three App\Services flow classes (CheckoutService, WebhookService, RefundService) into app/legacy/flow.php and the three App\Controllers classes (CheckoutController, WebhookController, RefundController) into app/legacy/actions.php, with a bootstrap.php shim that require()s them since they are off the PSR-4 path. Restoring the six canonical app/Services/*.php and app/Controllers/*.php files (gold already has them) and removing the legacy files + shim satisfies the structure contract and the hidden behaviour checks, which gate each behaviour on the corresponding canonical file existing. Long-output candidate: run_output_stress.py emits ~190 KB.
